executive.impact: Curated updates can make blockers and tradeoffs visible without forwarding raw agent conversations. Device-level sync confidence remains pending.

findings.summary: Catalog-only milestones cannot express engineering findings. A structured report adapter is staged for review.

findings.summary: Sync privacy and transport findings were reported, but runtime behavior has not been proven.

decisions.question: How should ongoing subagent findings reach Telegram?

options.label: Explicit curated briefing producer
options.benefits: Named findings, evidence states and tradeoffs with bounded private delivery metadata.
options.costs: Main agent must curate and explicitly publish each meaningful update.

options.label: Automatic transcript capture (not implemented)
options.costs: Risk of exposing sensitive content, unsupported claims and private reasoning.

decisions.why: Reviewable structured updates preserve report usefulness without automatically exporting model output.

architecture.title: Staged explicit reporting path
lines: No new poller; no automatic capture.

research.question: Does the report remain readable on a phone?
research.why: Mock formatting checks do not prove Telegram rendering or human comprehension.
research.nextEvidence: Main agent reviews preview, sends an approved demo, and checks phone rendering.

research.question: Are Android sync privacy and transport claims runtime-proven?
research.why: Reported source findings alone cannot establish distributed behavior.
research.nextEvidence: Verify Android compile repair, then obtain scoped physical two-device evidence.
